content.text: Does one logic govern all reasoning? Some say logic is universal. Others say different subjects need different logics.

content.definition: The view that more than one logic can be correct, each for its own purpose.

examples.title: Everyday if
lines: 'If you mow the lawn, I will pay you.' You do not mow it.
examples.note: Classically, the if then sentence is now true. In ordinary speech, the offer simply lapses.

examples.title: Many logics
examples.note: A pluralist accepts each in its place.

options: There is only one correct logic
Different purposes may need different logics
question.explanation: Pluralists hold that there is no single true logic. Different purposes may rightly use different logics.
